profile.behavior: Diurnal, mostly resident, and often territorial. Forages mainly on the ground, alone or in pairs, eating seeds, grains, fruit, and occasional small invertebrates. Pairs share incubation and chick care; adults may feign injury to draw predators away from nests.
field_marks: Warm cinnamon-brown head and rosy-brown underparts with a gray-brown back
Iridescent violet neck patch and small dark blue-black marks on the face
Several bold black spots on the wing coverts
White outer secondaries forming a pale trailing wing edge
Short, rounded tail with a dark subterminal band and white outer tips
Slim dark bill, large dark eye, and pinkish-red legs
profile.habitat: Open and semi-open habitats, especially lowland scrub, fields, forest edges, dense vegetation, coastal vegetation, mangroves, farmland, parks, and gardens.

findings: The primary specimen is a convincing Zenaida Dove: stocky dove proportions, warm cinnamon and rosy-brown plumage, gray-brown back, violet neck iridescence, dark facial mark, spotted wing coverts, pale secondary edge, rounded banded tail, slim dark bill, dark eye, and reddish legs agree with the reference photographs.

The primary specimen is anatomically coherent, with one head and bill, two legs, a single tail, and normally overlapping folded wings; the detached wing and head are clearly separated supplementary studies rather than additional birds or parts attached to the specimen.

Both depicted heads have consistent, slender bill proportions and compatible mandible projection. Neither bill looks truncated, reversed, forked, or materially exaggerated relative to the clearest side-profile reference.
The detached wing study independently preserves the spotted coverts, dark flight feathers, and conspicuous white trailing-edge marking characteristic of the species.

All visible identification, taxonomy, measurement, habitat, behavior, field-mark, and palette text is legible and correctly spelled. No duplicated, omitted, substituted, or nonsensical wording was found.
